text: The KovilAR application implements a structured four-phase pedagogical design following a learn-then-test approach. Users progress sequentially from guided orientation through holistic exploration and detailed inspection, culminating in a gamified spatial assessment. Each phase builds upon the preceding one, reinforcing domain knowledge through increasingly active interaction modalities.

Fig. 4–8 illustrate the four phases as experienced through the HoloLens 2 display. The journey begins with a draggable Reader Tab that introduces architectural terminology (Fig. 5), then transitions to a fully manipulable holographic reconstruction of the temple complex (Fig. 5). Users subsequently examine individual architectural components with contextual tooltips and spatial audio narrations (Fig. 5), guided by a mutual-exclusion audio controller (Fig. 5). Finally, the application challenges users to reconstruct the temple from scattered pieces in a 3D jigsaw puzzle (Fig. 5), with a layered system architecture (Fig. 5) coordinating input, manipulation, alignment validation, and multimodal feedback across all phases.

Implemented using the MRTK Slate component, the Reader Tab provides a draggable in-view panel that presents terminology definitions for key structural elements:

text: A SolverHandler component is attached to the Reader Tab to maintain spatial coherence with the user’s viewpoint. As the user physically moves through the environment, the solver continuously repositions the panel to remain within the field of view, ensuring that reference material is always accessible without occluding the primary 3D content. This design decision addresses a common challenge in MR educational applications: balancing supplementary information access with unobstructed spatial exploration.

runs.text: Phase 1: Reader Tab — MRTK Slate panel displaying Dravidian architectural terminology on HoloLens 2.

text: In the second phase, users explore the complete digital reconstruction of the Moovar Kovil temple complex. The 36-mesh hierarchical model — produced in Stage 1 of the development pipeline — is presented as a single interactive hologram in the HoloLens 2 field of view.

User interaction with the temple model is managed through the ObjectManipulator and ConstraintManager components (Section III-C), enabling constrained one-handed and two-handed manipulation. Y-axis rotation is fully free, allowing users to examine the temple from all horizontal perspectives — mirroring how one walks around a physical temple — while X and Z axes are locked to preserve upright orientation. Voice narrations recorded by a domain-expert faculty member accompany each structural level, providing contextual descriptions of architectural significance, historical provenance, and construction technique.

runs.text: Phase 2: Temple Exploration — interactive Moovar Kovil hologram with constrained-axis manipulation on HoloLens 2.

text: The third phase isolates individual architectural elements for focused study. Four primary components -- Pada (base), Gopuram (entrance tower), Adhisthanam (platform), and Vimana (sanctum tower) -- are presented separately, each with a gaze-triggered floating label and a dedicated spatial audio narration.

system. Each architectural element is linked to a floating

label (41 pt, centred alignment) via a Bezier-curved line connector rendered with 12 waypoints. The curved connector visually links the label to its component without the cluttered appearance of straight-line pointers -- important when multiple tooltips are visible simultaneously. Activation is gaze-triggered: when eye gaze dwells on an element the corresponding tooltip fades in, preventing information overload. Labels combine the Sanskrit architectural term with a contextual English gloss (e.g., Nandi - Lord Shiva's Vahanam), bridging domain-specific vocabulary with accessible description.

This pre-emptive stop enforces a single-channel audio policy, ensuring that only one educational narration is delivered at a time. The design follows multimedia learning principles—coordinating visual inspection with a single auditory channel—to manage cognitive load and improve retention compared to simultaneous multi-stream presentation.
Audio narration flow: mutual-exclusion controller enforcing single-channel playback per selected component.

text: The final phase transforms learning into active assessment through a 3D spatial jigsaw puzzle. Temple sections are scattered in the user's environment and must be translated and rotated into their correct spatial positions. The puzzle validation pipeline is built on the BoxCollider trigger zones introduced in Section III, each zone governed by a custom alignment script -- TriggerBase, TriggerFront, and TriggerMiddle -- that together implement the full assessment logic.

When the AND condition holds, the completion sequence activates: (1) a sacred ShivLingam object, initially hidden in the scene hierarchy, is revealed; (2) a golden material (MRTK Standard shader with hover-light responsiveness) is applied to the Renderer components of all assembled pieces, producing a visually distinct transformation; and (3) a devotional audio track plays through the spatial audio system. If any piece subsequently exits its trigger zone, the coordinator reverses the entire sequence—hiding the ShivLingam, restoring the default material, and stopping audio—ensuring that the completion reward remains contingent on maintaining correct assembly.

text: Repeatability is a critical requirement for educational applications, where multiple users or successive learning attempts must begin from a consistent initial state. KovilAR implements a two-tier reset architecture that separates scene-level state restoration from puzzle-specific state management.

text: This separation allows instructors or users to reset the puzzle independently—returning pieces to their scattered positions for another assembly attempt—without disturbing the broader scene state, or to perform a full scene reset that reinitialises the entire experience. The two-tier design thus supports both iterative puzzle practice within a single session and complete state restoration between successive users.
